messages:
Alex: Quick heads-up — after deploying mixed-precision kernels (FP8 for matmul, INT8 for attention) on the continuous-batching path, we're seeing two reg flags: padding waste up ~18% and KV cache miss rate spiked.
Maya: ugh. what's the batch shape distribution? :thinking_face: 
Alex: 90% short sequences (<64), but batching window is 200ms so we end up grouping variable-length requests. profiler dump:
```
kernel_select: fp8_matmul_v3 preferred for shapes >= (128,128)
observed_shapes: [(12,64)x40, (32,64)x30, (128,128)x2]
padding_waste: 18.2%
kv_cache_miss: 6.5% -> 14.9% post-mix
latency_p50: +12ms
```
Mike: That kernel_select line is the clue. FP8 matmul kernel has alignment restrictions — it pads to 128 on one dim which kills short-seq efficiency.
Tanaka: Also mixed precision transforms kv packing layout, so cache lookup key size changed? Can you paste the alloc stack and the cache key hash function used.
Alex: here's the cache key snippet we run in runtime:
```
key = sha256(model_id || layer_idx || sequence_len || kv_dtype)
```
Maya: kv_dtype toggles between bfloat16/int8/fp8 during calibration. If dtype flips, cache misses are expected. We probably recompiled kernels with different dtype and didn't normalize the key.
Alex: oh wow. so the key includes dtype. That explains the misses. But padding waste remains.
Mike: For padding fix, two options: 1) enforce dynamic kernel selection that prefers small-shape kernels for sequence<64, 2) trim pad by grouping by seq_len buckets at enqueue.
Tanaka: bucketed enqueue seems best low-risk: small extra latency on enqueuing but avoids wide padding. Could add a soft timer to avoid head-of-line blocking.
Alex: I'll try a prototype: bucket sizes [1-16,17-32,33-64,65-128] and prefer int8/4bit kernels for the smallest buckets. Quick config patch:
```
batcher:
  strategy: bucketed
  buckets: [16,32,64,128]
  timeout_ms: 80
kernel_policy:
  - seq_lt: 33 -> kernel: int4_matmul_small
  - seq_lt: 65 -> kernel: int8_matmul_small
  - else -> fp8_matmul_v3
```
Maya: also add a cache key normalization step: map equivalent dtypes (fp8_a, fp8_b) to 'fp8' base, and treat quantized variants as same bucket for caching.
Alex: good call. I'll commit that.
infra-bot: deploy-started: rolling update to runtime/v3.2 with bucketed-batcher experiment (canary 10%).
Mike: while canary runs, can you gather per-bucket padding waste and kv_miss metrics? add these prometheus labels: bucket_size, kernel_chosen, kv_key_version.
Tanaka: FYI if the int4 kernel uses different kernel shape constraints we'll need to adjust tiling in matmul op to avoid warp underutilization.
Alex: noted. I'll add perf counters and flamegraphs.
Maya: thanks. If this reduces padding_waste to <5% and kv_miss to baseline, we can roll out. Otherwise rollback.
Alex: will report back in ~30m with metrics. :thumbsup: 
infra-bot: deploy-success: canary 10% stable after 6m. metrics collected.
Alex: quick numbers from canary:
```
bucket 16: padding_waste 3.1%, kv_miss 2.1%, p50 -2ms
bucket 32: padding_waste 4.5%, kv_miss 2.4%, p50 -1ms
bucket 64: padding_waste 6.9%, kv_miss 3.2%, p50 +1ms
overall padding_waste: 4.9% (was 18.2%)
overall kv_miss: 2.8% (was 14.9%)
```
Maya: woo! nice.
Mike: great. open an ops-runbook note about kernel dtype normalization and include a test that increments a fake dtype list and ensures cache hits.
Alex: will do. Creating issue: runtime#1289 with tags perf, kv, batcher.
Tanaka: also schedule a perf regression test for mixed-precision toggles.
Alex: done. closing thread, will follow up with PRs.
